q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Prorogation of a House of Parliament by the President brings a session of the House to a close.
2. Bills pending before a House do not lapse on account of the prorogation of the House.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Prorogation by the President terminates a session of the House, and under parliamentary rules Bills pending before the House do not lapse on prorogation, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution.
2. One-third of the members of the Rajya Sabha retire on the expiration of every second year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House not subject to dissolution, and one-third of its members retire on expiration of every second year under Article 83, so both statements are correct.

q: The disqualification of a member of a Legislature on the ground of defection is dealt with in the Constitution in:

options.A: The Ninth Schedule
options.B: The Eighth Schedule
options.C: The Tenth Schedule
options.D: The Seventh Schedule

e: Disqualification on ground of defection is dealt with in the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution, inserted by the Fifty-second Amendment, commonly called the anti-defection law.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'uniform price' auction of Government securities from a 'multiple price' auction?

options.A: In a uniform price auction all securities are sold to a single bidder, while in a multiple price auction they are sold to many bidders
options.B: In a uniform price auction the securities are issued at a discount, while in a multiple price auction they are issued at a premium
options.C: A uniform price auction is used only for Treasury Bills, while a multiple price auction is used only for dated securities
options.D: In a uniform price auction all successful bidders pay the same cut-off price or yield, while in a multiple price auction each successful bidder pays the price or yield quoted by him

e: In a uniform price auction all successful bidders pay the same cut-off price or yield, while in a multiple price auction each successful bidder pays the price or yield quoted by him.

q: The primary dealers in the Government securities market primarily undertake:

options.A: The audit of the public debt of the Government of India
options.B: The fixation of the interest rates on Government securities
options.C: The printing and custody of Government securities
options.D: Underwriting of, and market making in, Government securities, supporting their issuance and trading

e: Primary dealers primarily undertake underwriting of, and market making in, Government securities, supporting their issuance, distribution and trading in the market.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on nutrition is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Under the List of Major and Minor Heads, revenue expenditure on Nutrition is accounted for under Major Head 2236; 2235 is Social Security and Welfare and 2230 is Labour and Employment.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on plantations is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Revenue expenditure on Plantations is accounted for under Major Head 2407 in the List of Major Heads; 2401 is Crop Husbandry, 2415 Agricultural Research and 2425 Co-operation.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts of the Government from education, sports, art and culture are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Receipts from Education, Sports, Art and Culture are accounted for under Major Head 0202, a tax and non-tax revenue receipt head, distinct from expenditure heads for these services.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts of the Government from medical and public health are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Receipts from Medical and Public Health are accounted for under Major Head 0210; 0202 covers Education, Sports, Art and Culture and 0215 covers Water Supply and Sanitation receipts.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on food storage and warehousing is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Capital Outlay on Food Storage and Warehousing is accounted for under Major Head 4408; 4401 is Capital Outlay on Crop Husbandry and 4406 is Capital Outlay on Forestry and Wildlife.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on co-operation is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Capital Outlay on Co-operation is accounted for under Major Head 4425; 4408 is Food Storage and Warehousing and 4435 is Capital Outlay on Other Agricultural Programmes.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on command area development is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Capital Outlay on Command Area Development is accounted for under Major Head 4705, separate from 4700 Major Irrigation, 4701 Medium Irrigation and 4702 Minor Irrigation capital heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on tourism is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Capital Outlay on Tourism is accounted for under Major Head 5452; 3452 is the corresponding revenue expenditure head for Tourism, the 5 series denoting capital outlay.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the loans given for dairy development are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Loans for Dairy Development are accounted for under Major Head 6404; 6403 is Loans for Animal Husbandry, 6405 Loans for Fisheries and 6401 Loans for Crop Husbandry.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the revenue expenditure on flood control projects is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Revenue expenditure on Flood Control Projects is accounted for under Major Head 2711, the revenue head for flood control, distinct from capital and other water resources heads.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the expenditure on the Secretariat under Social Services is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Secretariat expenditure under Social Services is accounted for under Major Head 2251, Secretariat - Social Services; 2051 covers Public Service Commission and 2235 Social Security.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the adjusting account with the Defence Services, used for inter-departmental adjustments with Defence, is accounted for under Major Head:
e: The adjusting account with Defence Services for inter-departmental adjustments with Defence is accounted for under Major Head 8789 in the Remittance section of the Public Account.

q: A surcharge levied by Parliament under Article 271 of the Constitution, for the purposes of the Union:

options.A: Forms part of the divisible pool of taxes to be shared with the States
options.B: Forms part of the Consolidated Fund of India, and its proceeds are not shareable with the States
options.C: Can be levied only on the recommendation of the Finance Commission
options.D: Is levied and collected by the State Governments on behalf of the Union

e: A surcharge under Article 271 forms part of the Consolidated Fund of India and its proceeds are not shareable with States, as Article 271 excludes it from the divisible pool.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Article 268 of the Constitution from Article 269?

options.A: Article 268 covers duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States, while Article 269 covers taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States
options.B: Article 268 covers taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States, while Article 269 covers duties levied by the Union but collected by the States
options.C: Article 268 relates to grants-in-aid to the States, while Article 269 relates to loans to the States
options.D: Article 268 relates to the taxes of the Union, while Article 269 relates to the taxes of the States alone

e: Article 268 covers duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by States, while Article 269 covers taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to States.

q: Appropriation Bills in the Legislature of a State, authorising appropriation out of the Consolidated Fund of the State of the moneys required to meet the grants and the charged expenditure, are provided for in the Constitution under:

options.A: Article 202
options.B: Article 203
options.C: Article 204
options.D: Article 205

e: Article 204 provides for Appropriation Bills in a State Legislature authorising appropriation from the Consolidated Fund of the State of moneys for grants and charged expenditure.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Article 285 of the Constitution from Article 289?

options.A: Article 285 exempts the income of the States from Union taxation, while Article 289 exempts the property of the Union from State taxation
options.B: Article 285 relates to the property of the States, while Article 289 relates to the property of the Union
options.C: Both Articles relate only to the exemption of railway property from taxation
options.D: Article 285 exempts the property of the Union from all taxes imposed by a State or an authority within a State, while Article 289 exempts the property and income of a State from Union taxation

e: Article 285 exempts property of the Union from taxes imposed by a State or authority within a State, while Article 289 exempts property and income of a State from Union taxation.

q: Under Article 299 of the Constitution, all contracts made in the exercise of the executive power of the Union or of a State are required to be:

options.A: Expressed to be made by the President, or by the Governor of the State, as the case may be
options.B: Registered with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: Approved in advance by the Legislature concerned
options.D: Executed only in the name of the Secretary of the Department concerned

e: Article 299 requires all contracts made in exercise of executive power of the Union or a State to be expressed to be made by the President or the Governor, as the case may be.

q: Article 300A of the Constitution, which provides that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law, has the effect that the right to property is now:

options.A: A fundamental right enforceable in the same manner as before its deletion from Part III
options.B: Available only to citizens, and not to other persons
options.C: Extinguished altogether, so that property may be taken without any law
options.D: A constitutional and legal right, though no longer a fundamental right

e: Article 300A, inserted after property was removed from Part III, makes right to property a constitutional and legal right, not a fundamental right, depriveable only by authority of law.

q: The Goods and Services Tax levied in India is, in its essential character, a:

options.A: Destination-based tax, levied at the point of consumption of goods and services
options.B: Origin-based tax, levied at the point of production of goods
options.C: Tax levied only at the first point of sale of goods
options.D: Tax levied exclusively on manufacturers

e: GST in India is a destination-based tax levied at the point of consumption, so revenue accrues to the consuming State, unlike an origin-based tax at point of production.

q: Under the 'dual GST' model adopted in India, a supply of goods or services made within a State is subjected to:

options.A: Only the Central Goods and Services Tax, levied by the Centre
options.B: Only the State Goods and Services Tax, levied by the State
options.C: Either the Central tax or the State tax, at the option of the supplier
options.D: The Central Goods and Services Tax and the State Goods and Services Tax, levied concurrently by the Centre and the State respectively

e: Under dual GST, an intra-State supply attracts CGST levied by the Centre and SGST levied by the State concurrently on the same transaction.

q: The Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) is the organisation which primarily:

options.A: Provides the information technology infrastructure and services for the implementation of the Goods and Services Tax, including the common GST portal
options.B: Fixes the rates of the Goods and Services Tax for all commodities
options.C: Conducts the audit of all dealers registered under the Goods and Services Tax
options.D: Collects the Goods and Services Tax in cash on behalf of the Governments

e: GSTN provides the information technology infrastructure and services for GST implementation, including the common GST portal for registration, returns and payments.

q: Under the Goods and Services Tax law, exports of goods and services are treated as:

options.A: Exempt supplies, on which no input tax credit is admissible
options.B: Supplies taxable at the standard rate applicable to domestic supplies
options.C: Supplies outside the scope of the tax altogether, like alcoholic liquor
options.D: Zero-rated supplies, so that the exporter may claim refund of the unutilised input tax credit or of the tax paid

e: Exports are zero-rated supplies under GST law, so the exporter may claim refund of unutilised input tax credit or of tax paid, unlike exempt supplies where credit is denied.

q: 'Unfunded debt' of the Government, in the classification of public debt followed in India, comprises:

options.A: The obligations of the Government accounted for in the Public Account, such as Provident Funds, deposits and reserve funds, which are repayable in due course but are not funded debt
options.B: Market loans raised by the Government for a fixed term
options.C: Treasury Bills issued for meeting temporary cash requirements
options.D: Loans raised by the Government from foreign Governments

e: Unfunded debt comprises Government obligations accounted for in the Public Account, such as Provident Funds, deposits and reserve funds, repayable in due course but not funded debt.

q: 'Earmarking' of a tax, in public finance, means:

options.A: Exempting a class of taxpayers from the payment of the tax
options.B: Postponing the collection of the tax to a later year
options.C: Merging the proceeds of the tax in the general revenues of the Government
options.D: Assigning the proceeds of the tax to be spent on a specified purpose or service

e: Earmarking of a tax means assigning its proceeds to be spent on a specified purpose or service, instead of merging them in general revenues available for all purposes.

q: The 'diffusion theory' of the incidence of taxation, associated with Canard, holds in essence that:

options.A: A tax tends, through a series of economic transactions and exchanges, to diffuse itself and spread its burden over the community as a whole
options.B: The burden of a tax always remains on the person on whom it is first imposed
options.C: Only direct taxes can be shifted, and indirect taxes cannot
options.D: The incidence of a tax can be determined solely from the statute imposing it

e: The diffusion theory of Canard holds that a tax tends, through a series of transactions and exchanges, to diffuse itself and spread its burden over the community as a whole.

q: Where a tax is levied on a commodity, the division of its money burden between the buyer and the seller depends principally on:

options.A: The person on whom the tax is statutorily imposed
options.B: The authority which collects the tax
options.C: The name given to the tax in the statute
options.D: The relative elasticities of demand for, and supply of, the commodity taxed

e: Where a tax is levied on a commodity, division of its money burden between buyer and seller depends principally on relative elasticities of demand and supply of the commodity.

q: The principle of 'vertical equity' in taxation requires that:

options.A: Taxpayers who are in unequal economic circumstances should be treated unequally, the better-placed bearing a larger burden
options.B: All taxpayers should pay the tax at one uniform rate, whatever their circumstances
options.C: Taxpayers in equal circumstances should be taxed equally
options.D: The tax burden should fall only on persons with no income

e: Vertical equity requires taxpayers in unequal circumstances to be treated unequally, the better-placed bearing a larger burden, unlike horizontal equity for equals.

q: In the Government system of accounts, the heads of account other than those relating to revenue and capital expenditure within the Consolidated Fund are collectively known as:

options.A: Link heads
options.B: Suspense heads
options.C: Pro forma heads
options.D: Debt, Deposit and Remittance heads

e: Heads other than revenue and capital expenditure heads within the Consolidated Fund are collectively Debt, Deposit and Remittance heads, covering Public Account and remittance transactions.

q: Treasury Bills issued by the Government of India are, in their nature:

options.A: Short-term instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at par, carrying no coupon interest
options.B: Long-term instruments carrying a fixed rate of interest payable half-yearly
options.C: Instruments which can be held only by the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: Perpetual securities with no date of redemption

e: Treasury Bills are short-term instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at par, carrying no coupon interest; the return is the difference between issue and redemption price.

q: The divisible pool of the net proceeds of taxes, which is shared between the Union and the States on the recommendations of the Finance Commission, does NOT include:

options.A: Corporation tax
options.B: Taxes on income other than corporation tax
options.C: Customs duties forming part of the shareable taxes
options.D: A cess levied for specific purposes and a surcharge levied under Article 271, whose proceeds go entirely to the Union

e: The divisible pool shared on Finance Commission recommendations excludes cess for specific purposes and surcharge under Article 271, whose proceeds go entirely to the Union.

q: A 'calling attention' notice in Parliament enables a member to:

options.A: Move a motion of no-confidence in the Council of Ministers
options.B: Call the attention of a Minister to a matter of urgent public importance, on which the Minister makes a statement
options.C: Raise a point of order on the proceedings of the House
options.D: Demand the adjournment of the business of the House for the day

e: A calling attention notice enables a member to call attention of a Minister to a matter of urgent public importance, on which the Minister makes a statement.

q: A 'half-an-hour discussion' in the Lok Sabha is a discussion:

options.A: Held for exactly half an hour on the Budget as a whole
options.B: On the report of the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: On a matter of sufficient public importance which has been the subject of a recent question, held during the last half hour of a sitting
options.D: On a Bill after its introduction in the House

e: A half-an-hour discussion is on a matter of sufficient public importance which has been subject of a recent question, held during the last half hour of a sitting.

q: A 'point of order' raised by a member in the House relates to:

options.A: A matter of general public importance requiring the attention of a Minister
options.B: The interpretation or enforcement of the rules of procedure of the House, or of the constitutional provisions regulating its business, on which the decision of the presiding officer is sought
options.C: A question of privilege of a member of the House
options.D: The allocation of time for the discussion of the Demands for Grants

e: A point of order relates to interpretation or enforcement of rules of procedure or constitutional provisions regulating House business, on which the presiding officer decision is sought.

q: A 'closure' motion in the House is a motion moved by a member:

options.A: To adjourn the House sine die
options.B: To refer a Bill to a Select Committee of the House
options.C: That the debate on the matter under discussion be closed and the question be now put to the vote of the House
options.D: To reduce the amount of a Demand for Grant under discussion

e: A closure motion is moved that debate on the matter under discussion be closed and the question be now put to vote of the House, curtailing further discussion if accepted.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'substantive motion' from a 'subsidiary motion'?

options.A: A substantive motion can be moved only by a Minister, while a subsidiary motion can be moved only by a private member
options.B: A substantive motion is a self-contained proposal which expresses the decision or opinion of the House, while a subsidiary motion depends upon, and arises out of, another motion or proceeding of the House
options.C: A substantive motion is never put to the vote, while a subsidiary motion always is
options.D: There is no difference between the two kinds of motions

e: A substantive motion is a self-contained proposal expressing decision or opinion of the House, while a subsidiary motion depends upon and arises out of another motion or proceeding.

q: The Committee on Petitions of the Lok Sabha primarily examines:

options.A: The estimates of expenditure of the Ministries
options.B: The reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: Petitions presented to the House on Bills and on matters of general public importance
options.D: The rules made by the Government under Acts of Parliament

e: The Committee on Petitions of Lok Sabha primarily examines petitions presented to the House on Bills and on matters of general public importance and reports thereon.

q: Audit evidence obtained directly from independent sources outside the audited entity is generally regarded as:

options.A: Less reliable than evidence generated within the entity itself
options.B: More reliable than evidence obtained from within the entity
options.C: Of no value for the purposes of audit
options.D: Usable only in the audit of Government companies

e: Audit evidence from independent sources outside the audited entity is generally more reliable than evidence generated within the entity, because it is free from entity bias and control.

q: Which of the following is NOT a component of internal control in an organisation?

options.A: The control environment
options.B: Risk assessment by the management
options.C: Statutory audit of the accounts by an external auditor
options.D: Monitoring of controls by the management

e: Statutory audit by an external auditor is not a component of internal control; components are control environment, risk assessment, information, control activities and monitoring.

q: A recognised inherent limitation of even a well-designed system of internal control is that it cannot provide absolute assurance against irregularities, principally because of:

options.A: The use of computers in maintaining the accounts
options.B: The possibility of collusion among employees and of the management overriding the controls
options.C: The absence of a written accounts manual in the office
options.D: The conduct of audit by test checks instead of cent-per-cent checks

e: Even a well-designed internal control cannot give absolute assurance because of inherent limits such as collusion among employees and management override of controls.

q: A zonal railway records an Operating Ratio of 104 per cent for a year. This position indicates that:

options.A: The railway has earned a net revenue equal to 4 per cent of its gross traffic earnings
options.B: The dividend payable by the railway is 4 per cent of its capital-at-charge
options.C: The gross working expenses of the railway have exceeded its gross traffic earnings, so that its net revenue is negative
options.D: The capital-at-charge of the railway has increased by 4 per cent during the year

e: Operating Ratio of 104 per cent means gross working expenses exceeded gross traffic earnings by 4 per cent of earnings, so net revenue is negative for the year.

q: A worn-out asset of a railway is renewed and replaced, and the cost of the renewal is financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund. The effect of this transaction on the capital-at-charge of the railway is that:

options.A: The capital-at-charge remains unchanged, as a renewal financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund does not add to it
options.B: The capital-at-charge increases by the full cost of the renewal
options.C: The capital-at-charge decreases by the cost of the renewal
options.D: The capital-at-charge increases by the difference between the cost of the new asset and the original cost of the old asset

e: Renewal financed from Depreciation Reserve Fund replaces a worn-out asset without adding to capital-at-charge, so capital-at-charge remains unchanged by that renewal.

q: An officer sanctions, in favour of a firm in which he is himself interested, a work to be executed for his office, at rates favourable to the firm. Apart from any other rule that may be attracted, the sanction offends against the canon of financial propriety that:

options.A: Expenditure should not be incurred to meet a demand likely to recur
options.B: Public moneys should be spent with the vigilance of a person spending his own money
options.C: A rush of expenditure should be avoided in the closing months of the year
options.D: No authority should exercise its power to sanction expenditure so as to pass an order which will be directly or indirectly to its own advantage

e: Canon of financial propriety bars an authority from exercising sanction power so as to pass an order directly or indirectly to its own advantage, as with a firm in which it is interested.

q: The cost of a survey carried out for a proposed new railway line is initially met from public funds. The line is thereafter sanctioned and constructed. In the railway accounts, the cost of that survey is properly treated as:

options.A: Part of the capital cost of the project, the survey having been undertaken for a work which was actually taken up
options.B: A charge to revenue in all cases, surveys being of a revenue nature
options.C: A charge to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: An item to be held permanently under a suspense head

e: Survey cost for a proposed line that is thereafter sanctioned and constructed forms part of capital cost of the project, the survey having been for a work actually taken up.

q: Expenditure on a service is, through an error of classification, booked against the grant of another Ministry, and the mistake is noticed by Audit after the accounts are closed. The correct position is that:

options.A: The error is of no consequence, since the total expenditure of the Government as a whole is unchanged
options.B: The expenditure stands automatically regularised by the savings available under the other grant
options.C: The booking under a wrong grant vitiates the authorisation given by Parliament for that grant, and the amount is treated as an excess over the grant to which it properly belonged, requiring regularisation
options.D: The amount is transferred to the Public Account of India and the matter closed

e: Booking expenditure under a wrong grant vitiates Parliament authorisation for that grant; the amount is treated as excess over the grant to which it properly belonged, requiring regularisation.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'value of service' principle from the 'cost of service' principle in the fixation of railway rates?

options.A: The value of service principle bases the charge on the cost incurred in rendering the service, while the cost of service principle bases it on the capacity of the traffic to bear the charge
options.B: The value of service principle bases the charge on what the traffic can bear, that is, the value of the service to the user, while the cost of service principle bases it on the cost incurred in rendering the service
options.C: Both principles base the charge solely on the distance over which the traffic is carried
options.D: The value of service principle applies only to passenger traffic, and the cost of service principle only to goods traffic

e: Value of service bases railway charge on what traffic can bear, that is value to the user, while cost of service bases it on cost incurred in rendering the service.

q: Under Article 266(3) of the Constitution, moneys may be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India only:

options.A: On the orders of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Under appropriation made by law
options.C: On the authorisation of the Finance Minister
options.D: Against the Demands for Grants as presented to Parliament

e: Article 266(3) provides that no moneys shall be appropriated out of the Consolidated Fund of India except in accordance with law, i.e. under an Appropriation Act passed by Parliament.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'grant' from an 'appropriation' in the budgetary procedure of the Union?

options.A: A grant relates to charged expenditure, while an appropriation relates to voted expenditure
options.B: A grant is made by the Rajya Sabha, while an appropriation is made by the Lok Sabha
options.C: A grant is the amount voted by the Lok Sabha on a Demand, while an appropriation is the amount authorised by the Appropriation Act for issue from the Consolidated Fund of India, covering both voted grants and charged expenditure
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms

e: A grant is the sum voted by Lok Sabha on a Demand for Grant, whereas appropriation is the sum authorised by the Appropriation Act for issue from the Consolidated Fund, covering voted grants and charged expenditure.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Finance Act from the Appropriation Act?

options.A: The Finance Act gives legal effect to the taxation and financial proposals of the Budget, while the Appropriation Act authorises withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the grants and charged expenditure
options.B: The Finance Act is passed only by the Rajya Sabha, while the Appropriation Act is passed only by the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Finance Act authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India, while the Appropriation Act levies taxes
options.D: The Finance Act is presented after the Appropriation Act in every session

e: The Finance Act gives legal effect to the taxation proposals of the Budget, while the Appropriation Act authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund to meet voted grants and charged expenditure.

q: The word 'Budget' does not occur in the Constitution of India. The document presented annually to Parliament, popularly called the Budget, is referred to in the Constitution as the:

options.A: Demands for Grants
options.B: Finance Bill
options.C: Appropriation Statement
options.D: Annual Financial Statement

e: The Constitution does not use the word Budget. Article 112 calls the annual statement of estimated receipts and expenditure laid before Parliament the Annual Financial Statement.

q: Which of the following items of expenditure is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: Salaries and allowances of the Members of Parliament
options.B: Pensions of the Judges of the High Courts
options.C: Salaries of the staff of the Railway Board
options.D: Grants-in-aid given to the State Governments

e: Pensions of High Court Judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 112(3), so they are not submitted to the vote of Parliament.

q: Re-appropriation of funds in the Union Budget is NOT permissible:

options.A: From a capital head to a revenue head, or vice versa
options.B: Within the same grant, between two revenue heads
options.C: Between two minor heads under the same grant, with competent sanction
options.D: From one unit of appropriation to another within the same grant, subject to the prescribed restrictions

e: Re-appropriation is allowed only within the same grant and subject to restrictions. Transfer from a capital head to a revenue head or vice versa is expressly prohibited.

q: An administrative department seeks to re-appropriate funds from a grant in the month of April following the close of the financial year to which the grant related. The correct position is that:

options.A: The re-appropriation is valid if sanctioned by the Finance Ministry
options.B: The re-appropriation is valid if the amount is small
options.C: No re-appropriation can be made after the close of the financial year, as the grant of that year has lapsed
options.D: The re-appropriation can be made with the approval of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: All grants lapse at the close of the financial year to which they relate. Hence no re-appropriation can be made in April in respect of the grant of the previous year.

q: The 'monetised deficit' of the Government for a year broadly represents:

options.A: The fiscal deficit minus the interest payments of the year
options.B: The revenue deficit minus grants for the creation of capital assets
options.C: The excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts
options.D: The increase in the net credit of the Reserve Bank of India to the Government, representing the money-financed portion of the deficit

e: Monetised deficit is the increase in net RBI credit to Government during the year, i.e. the portion of the fiscal deficit financed by creation of money through the central bank.

q: 'Deficit financing', in the context of Government budgets, ordinarily denotes:

options.A: Financing the budgetary deficit through borrowing and creation of money
options.B: Meeting revenue expenditure entirely out of revenue receipts
options.C: Financing capital works only through market borrowings
options.D: Reducing the fiscal deficit by disinvestment of public enterprises

e: Deficit financing ordinarily means financing the overall budgetary deficit by borrowing, including creation of money, when receipts fall short of expenditure.

q: A 'sinking fund' maintained by a Government serves the purpose of:

options.A: Meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by the Legislature
options.B: Providing a fund, built up by periodical contributions, for the redemption of public debt on maturity
options.C: Holding the deposits of Government servants
options.D: Financing the ways and means advances to the States

e: A sinking fund is built up by periodical contributions so that a sufficient sum is available to redeem or repay public debt on its maturity.

q: The 'floating debt' of the Government of India broadly comprises:

options.A: Loans raised in the external market
options.B: Provident Fund balances of Government servants
options.C: Short-term borrowings, such as Treasury Bills and Ways and Means Advances from the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: Long-term market loans of twenty years and above

e: Floating debt consists of short-term borrowings of Government, such as treasury bills and Ways and Means Advances from the Reserve Bank of India.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'internal debt' from 'external debt' of the Government of India?

options.A: Internal debt is repayable within one year, while external debt is repayable after one year
options.B: Internal debt is owed to the Reserve Bank of India only, while external debt is owed to the States
options.C: Internal debt comprises borrowings raised within the country, while external debt comprises borrowings raised outside the country
options.D: Internal debt is accounted for in the Public Account, while external debt is accounted for in the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Internal debt is borrowing raised within the country, while external debt is borrowing raised outside the country, the distinction resting on the source and residence of the lender.

q: The canon of convenience in taxation, enunciated by Adam Smith, requires that:

options.A: Every subject should contribute in proportion to his ability
options.B: The cost of collecting a tax should be as small as possible
options.C: The tax payable by each person should be certain and not arbitrary
options.D: Every tax should be levied at the time, and in the manner, most convenient for the contributor to pay it

e: Under Adam Smith's canon of convenience, every tax should be levied at the time and in the manner in which it is most likely to be convenient for the contributor to pay it.

q: The canon of economy in taxation requires that:

options.A: The tax should be payable at a time convenient to the taxpayer
options.B: The yield of the tax should increase automatically with national income
options.C: The cost of collecting the tax should be small in proportion to its yield, and the tax should not discourage industry
options.D: The tax should fall equally on all taxpayers

e: The canon of economy requires that the cost of collecting a tax should be small compared with its yield and that the tax should not discourage industry or check enterprise.

q: 'Backward shifting' of a tax takes place when the person on whom the tax is imposed shifts its burden:

options.A: Onto the buyers of his product through higher prices
options.B: Onto the suppliers of his inputs or his employees, through lower prices or lower wages
options.C: Onto the Government through a subsidy
options.D: Onto future generations through public borrowing

e: In backward shifting the taxed person shifts the burden backwards to his suppliers or employees by paying lower input prices or lower wages, instead of charging buyers more.

q: 'Seigniorage' in public finance refers to:

options.A: The interest earned by the Reserve Bank of India on foreign securities
options.B: The profit arising to the State from a surcharge on income tax
options.C: The revenue obtained by the Government from escheated property
options.D: The gain accruing to the issuing authority from the issue of money, being broadly the excess of its face value over the cost of its production

e: Seigniorage is the gain to the issuing authority from issuing money, broadly the excess of the face value of coins or currency over the cost of producing it.

q: The 'golden rule' of public finance, relating to Government borrowing, lays down that:

options.A: Government should borrow only for investment and capital purposes, and meet current expenditure out of current revenue
options.B: Government should borrow only from the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Government borrowing should never exceed the revenue receipts of the year
options.D: Government should borrow only in years of surplus in the revenue account

e: The golden rule of public finance requires Government to meet current or revenue expenditure from current revenue and to borrow only for investment and capital purposes.

q: The 'cascading effect' of an indirect tax arises when:

options.A: The tax is shifted forward more than once
options.B: Tax is levied, at successive stages of production and distribution, on a price which already includes the tax paid at an earlier stage, resulting in tax on tax
options.C: The tax is levied at a progressively higher rate at higher incomes
options.D: The tax is collected at source by the seller

e: Cascading occurs when tax is charged at successive stages on a value that already includes tax paid earlier, producing a tax-on-tax effect in the final price.

q: In audit, 'detection risk' refers to the risk that:

options.A: The financial statements contain a material misstatement before audit
options.B: The internal control system fails to prevent a material misstatement
options.C: The audit procedures performed will fail to detect a material misstatement that exists
options.D: The sample selected is not representative of the population

e: Detection risk is the risk that the auditor's procedures will fail to detect a material misstatement that exists in the financial statements.

q: 'Materiality' in audit refers to a matter whose:

options.A: Amount exceeds the total grant of the audited unit
options.B: Omission or misstatement could influence the decisions of the users of the accounts or the conclusions drawn from the audit
options.C: Correction requires the sanction of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Detection is possible only through cent-per-cent check

e: A matter is material if its omission or misstatement could influence the economic decisions of users of the accounts or the conclusions drawn from audit.

q: The power of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India to inspect any office of accounts under the control of the Union or of a State, in connection with audit, is provided for in the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:

options.A: Section 18
options.B: Section 13
options.C: Section 10
options.D: Section 23

e: Section 18 of the CAG's Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service Act, 1971 empowers the CAG to inspect any office of accounts under the control of the Union or a State.

q: Under Section 20 of the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the audit of the accounts of a body or authority not otherwise covered by the Act may be undertaken by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India when:

options.A: The body requests a private auditor for the purpose
options.B: It is entrusted to him by the President or, as the case may be, the Governor of a State
options.C: The Public Accounts Committee directs him to do so
options.D: The body receives any grant from a State Government

e: Section 20 of the CAG's DPC Act, 1971 provides for audit of bodies or authorities not otherwise covered, when such audit is entrusted to the CAG by the President or the Governor.

q: The audit of the receipts and expenditure of bodies and authorities substantially financed by grants or loans from the Consolidated Fund of India is provided for in the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:

options.A: Section 16
options.B: Section 17
options.C: Section 14
options.D: Section 19

e: Section 14 of the CAG's DPC Act, 1971 deals with audit of receipts and expenditure of bodies and authorities substantially financed by grants or loans from the Consolidated Fund.

q: Before an audit paragraph is finally included in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, the draft paragraph is, in the normal course, forwarded to:

options.A: The Secretary of the Ministry or Department concerned, for obtaining and considering its comments
options.B: The Public Accounts Committee, for its prior approval
options.C: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha, for vetting
options.D: The Finance Minister, for editing

e: In normal audit procedure the draft paragraph is sent to the Secretary of the Ministry or Department concerned so that its comments are obtained and considered before finalisation.

q: Action Taken Notes furnished by a Ministry on the paragraphs in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are, before being placed before the Public Accounts Committee, ordinarily:

options.A: Approved by the Railway Convention Committee
options.B: Published in the Gazette of India
options.C: Countersigned by the Finance Minister
options.D: Vetted by the audit organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Action Taken Notes sent by a Ministry to the Public Accounts Committee are first vetted by the CAG's audit organisation to verify the facts and the action claimed.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes performance audit from compliance audit?

options.A: Performance audit is conducted by the Accounts Department, while compliance audit is conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Compliance audit examines conformity of transactions with rules, sanctions and authorities, while performance audit examines the economy, efficiency and effectiveness with which resources have been used
options.C: Performance audit is confined to arithmetical accuracy, while compliance audit covers programme outcomes
options.D: There is no difference between the two

e: Compliance audit tests conformity with rules, sanctions and authorities, while performance audit examines economy, efficiency and effectiveness in the use of resources, the three Es.

q: In the States, the compilation and maintenance of the accounts of the State Government (other than those relating to the departments whose accounts have been departmentalised) is carried out, under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, by:

options.A: The Controller General of Accounts
options.B: The State Finance Department
options.C: The Accountant General (Accounts and Entitlements) of the State
options.D: The Reserve Bank of India

e: State Government accounts, except for departmentalised departments, are compiled and maintained under the CAG by the Accountant General (Accounts and Entitlements) of the State.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is the head of:

options.A: The Indian Audit and Accounts Department
options.B: The Indian Civil Accounts Service
options.C: The Controller General of Accounts organisation
options.D: The Railway Accounts Department

e: The CAG is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department, through which he discharges his duties relating to accounts and audit under the Constitution and the DPC Act, 1971.

q: In respect of a Government company, a supplementary audit of its accounts may be conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India under the provisions of:

options.A: The General Financial Rules, 2017
options.B: The Railways Act, 1989
options.C: The Indian Audit and Accounts Service Rules
options.D: The Companies Act, 2013

e: Supplementary audit of a Government company by the CAG is conducted under the Companies Act, 2013, notably the provisions relating to audit of Government companies.

q: The Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB), which formulates accounting standards for the Union and State Governments, functions under the aegis of:

options.A: The Ministry of Finance
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Reserve Bank of India
options.D: The Controller General of Accounts

e: The Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board, which formulates accounting standards for Union and State Governments, functions under the aegis of the CAG of India.

q: The 'social service obligations' borne by Indian Railways broadly refer to:

options.A: The expenditure incurred by Railways on the staff benefit fund
options.B: The dividend relief claimed by Railways on strategic lines
options.C: The losses borne by Railways in providing services below cost, such as concessional passenger services and the working of uneconomic lines, in the discharge of social obligations
options.D: The contributions made by Railways to the Prime Minister's relief funds

e: Social service obligations are the losses Railways bear in providing services below cost, such as concessional passenger traffic and uneconomic lines, for social reasons.

q: On Indian Railways, the pensionary charges payable to retired railway staff are met from:

options.A: The Pension Fund, which is credited with appropriations from revenue
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India
options.C: The Capital Fund of Railways
options.D: The Public Account deposits of the subscribers

e: Pensionary charges of retired railway staff are met from the Pension Fund, to which appropriations are made from railway revenues to meet current pension payments.

q: Works chargeable to the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK) on Railways are, in their essential character:

options.A: Passenger amenity works at stations
options.B: Staff welfare and colony maintenance works
options.C: New line construction works taken up on commercial considerations
options.D: Safety-related works, such as renewal of track, bridges and signalling assets and elimination of level crossings

e: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh finances safety-related works, including renewal of track, bridges and signalling assets and elimination of level crossings.

q: In Government and Railway accounts, a 'transfer entry' is passed primarily in order to:

options.A: Transfer cash from one treasury to another
options.B: Transfer an amount from one head of account to another, so as to correct a misclassification or effect an adjustment in the accounts
options.C: Transfer a Government servant from one office to another
options.D: Transfer the balance of a grant to the next financial year

e: A transfer entry adjusts accounts by transferring an amount from one head to another, to correct misclassification or effect a proper adjustment, without any cash transaction.

q: In the terminology of Government accounts, an 'appropriation' signifies:

options.A: The total receipts of the Government during a year
options.B: The amount voted by the Lok Sabha on a Demand for Grant
options.C: The amount set apart, under the Appropriation Act, for expenditure on a specified service or purpose
options.D: The amount surrendered out of a grant at the close of the year

e: In budget terminology appropriation is the amount set apart under the Appropriation Act for expenditure on a specified service or purpose from the Consolidated Fund.

q: In the Lok Sabha, the allocation of time for the discussion of the Demands for Grants and other Government business is recommended by:

options.A: The Rules Committee of the Railway Board
options.B: The Estimates Committee
options.C: The Committee on Government Assurances
options.D: The Business Advisory Committee

e: The Business Advisory Committee of Lok Sabha recommends the allocation of time for discussion of Demands for Grants and other Government business in the House.

q: By a convention followed since 1967, the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament is ordinarily chosen from:

options.A: The ruling party in the Lok Sabha
options.B: The Rajya Sabha
options.C: The members of the Estimates Committee
options.D: The Opposition in the Lok Sabha

e: By convention followed since 1967, the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is ordinarily chosen from the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

q: An item outstanding under a suspense head of account can be finally cleared by writing it off to revenue or to another final head only:

options.A: Automatically, on the expiry of one year
options.B: Under the sanction of the authority competent to sanction such a write-off or adjustment
options.C: On the oral instructions of the head of office
options.D: At the time of the annual stock verification

e: A suspense item can be finally cleared by write-off to revenue or another final head only under sanction of the authority competent to sanction that write-off or adjustment.

q: The expression 'efficiency-cum-performance audit', used in the earlier audit practice of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, corresponds broadly to what is now known as:

options.A: Performance audit, covering economy, efficiency and effectiveness
options.B: Certification audit of the Finance Accounts
options.C: Local audit of a single office
options.D: Audit of stores and stock

e: The older term efficiency-cum-performance audit corresponds to modern performance audit, covering economy, efficiency and effectiveness of programmes and activities.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'inspection' of an office by the executive authorities from the statutory audit of that office?

options.A: Inspection is carried out by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, while audit is carried out by the head of office
options.B: Inspection and audit are identical in scope and authority
options.C: Inspection is a supervisory and administrative function of the executive, directed to the working of the office, while statutory audit is an independent examination conducted under the authority of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Inspection is concerned only with cash balances, while audit is concerned only with stores

e: Inspection is a supervisory administrative function of the executive over its offices, while statutory audit is an independent examination by or under the authority of the CAG.

q: Under Article 110 of the Constitution, a Bill is deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with, among other matters:

options.A: The salaries of the Members of Parliament
options.B: The appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The procedure for the election of the President
options.D: The imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax

e: Article 110 defines a Money Bill to include a Bill containing only provisions dealing with imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax, among other listed matters.

q: The provision of Article 108 of the Constitution for a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament is NOT available in the case of:

options.A: An ordinary Bill relating to a State subject
options.B: A Money Bill
options.C: A Bill relating to a Concurrent List subject
options.D: A Bill passed by one House and rejected by the other

e: Article 108 provides for a joint sitting in case of disagreement on ordinary Bills, but this procedure is expressly not available for a Money Bill.

q: A Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and transmitted to the Rajya Sabha must be returned by the Rajya Sabha, with or without its recommendations, within a period of:

options.A: Fourteen days from the date of its receipt
options.B: Six months from the date of its receipt
options.C: Thirty days from the date of its receipt
options.D: Seven days from the date of its receipt

e: Under Article 109, the Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill passed by Lok Sabha, with or without recommendations, within fourteen days of its receipt.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Commission is constituted by the President at the expiration of every fifth year, or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary.
2. A principal duty of the Finance Commission is to recommend the principles governing the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Article 280 requires the Finance Commission to be constituted every fifth year or earlier, and to recommend principles for distribution of net tax proceeds between Union and States. Both statements are correct.

q: The 'Budget at a Glance' document presented with the Union Budget primarily provides:

options.A: The detailed Demands for Grants of each Ministry
options.B: The text of the Finance Bill
options.C: The report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in summary form
options.D: A broad summary of the receipts and disbursements of the Government, showing the budgetary position and the principal deficit indicators

e: Budget at a Glance gives a broad summary of receipts and disbursements of Government, showing the budgetary position and the main deficit indicators in one place.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts of the Government from crop husbandry are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 0403 - Animal Husbandry
options.B: 0401 - Crop Husbandry
options.C: 0405 - Fisheries
options.D: 0406 - Forestry and Wild Life

e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads, receipts from crop husbandry are classified under Major Head 0401 - Crop Husbandry in the revenue receipts section.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts of the Government from forestry and wild life are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 0401 - Crop Husbandry
options.B: 0403 - Animal Husbandry
options.C: 0406 - Forestry and Wild Life
options.D: 0405 - Fisheries

e: Receipts from forestry and wild life are classified under Major Head 0406 - Forestry and Wild Life, as per the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts of the Government from power are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 0801 - Power
options.B: 0802 - Petroleum
options.C: 0803 - Coal and Lignite
options.D: 0853 - Non-ferrous Mining and Metallurgical Industries

e: Receipts from power are classified under Major Head 0801 - Power in the Government system of classification of accounts.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the receipts of the Government from road transport are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 1051 - Ports and Light Houses
options.B: 1052 - Shipping
options.C: 1053 - Civil Aviation
options.D: 1055 - Road Transport

e: Receipts from road transport are classified under Major Head 1055 - Road Transport, as per the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the capital outlay on agricultural research and education is accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 4401 - Capital Outlay on Crop Husbandry
options.B: 4415 - Capital Outlay on Agricultural Research and Education
options.C: 4403 - Capital Outlay on Animal Husbandry
options.D: 4425 - Capital Outlay on Co-operation

e: Capital outlay on agricultural research and education is classified under Major Head 4415 - Capital Outlay on Agricultural Research and Education.
